convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'ColorRsiMACD' custom indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trade execution and smoothing algorithms. Multi-mode signal logic with 4 different entry strategies.

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds for signal timestamp
min_rates_total - minimum bars needed for indicator warmup

other_exits: Signal-based close: opposite signal triggers close when BuyPosClose/SellPosClose enabled

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM input: negative=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction. MMMode=LOT means fixed lot sizing; when MM>0 and MMMode=LOT, 0.1 represents 10% of deposit for margin calculation

custom_logic_notes: Four selectable trading modes via AlgMode enum: (1) 'breakdown' - histogram crosses zero line; (2) 'MACDtwist' - MACD histogram direction change (decreasing to increasing = buy, increasing to decreasing = sell); (3) 'SIGNALtwist' - signal line direction change (same logic on buffer 2); (4) 'MACDdisposition' - MACD line crosses signal line. Uses previous bar values ([1],[2]) compared to earlier bars ([0]) for crossover detection with SignalBar offset. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose input booleans independently gate each direction's entry and exit. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose functions. GlobalVariableDel_ cleans up global variables on deinit.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement ColorRsiMACD custom indicator logic: RSI applied to custom price, then smoothed with T3 (fast/slow), then signal line with JJMA. SmoothAlgorithms.mqh contains non-standard smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) that need Python equivalents - consider ta-lib or custom implementations. TradeAlgorithms.mqh trading functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, etc.) must be replaced with broker API calls. The 4-mode switch logic is straightforward to translate. SignalBar=1 means signals are evaluated on the previous completed bar (shift 1), which is standard for bar-based strategies. No digit adjustment detected in SL/TP - the 1000/2000 pip values are used as-is, meaning they may be in points (not pips) and would need adjustment for 5-digit brokers (divide by 10 for pip-based systems).
